extracted.intended_audience: scientists, research workers, and readers of Nature (early-20th-century scientific community)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and observational standards for assessing the state and cycle of solar activity using sunspots, prominences, sunspot areas, latitudes, and the form of the corona derived from eclipse reports and published data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use multiple visible phenomena to determine solar activity
rubrics_metrics.description: The sun's variability can be determined from several different visible phenomena and not solely from the total integrated light emitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not treat the Sun as a regular variable based only on integrated light; combine observations of sunspots, prominences, and corona form to assess activity. Keep in mind the approximate eleven-year period is itself variable due to minor periods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mean heliographic latitude of sunspots (per hemisphere, yearly)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each point represents the mean heliographic latitude of all spots for each hemisphere throughout the whole year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plot separate latitude curves for northern and southern hemispheres and use yearly averages. Use the same data sources as for area curves; consult the published sources referenced (e.g., Astronomer Royal values) when compiling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mean daily areas of sunspots corrected for foreshortening (yearly means)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each point in the curve represents the mean of the daily areas of sunspots corrected for foreshortening for each year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the yearly values published by the Astronomer Royal in the Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society. Treat values for recent years that have been marked provisional (e.g., three later years marked with crosses) with caution.

rubrics_metrics.name: High-latitude outbursts herald new sunspot cycles (~22°)
rubrics_metrics.description: A new sunspot cycle is always heralded by outbursts of spots in zones of high latitudes (about 22°), while the zone of spots nearer the equator is dying out.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monitor latitude-distribution changes: appearance of new activity near ~22° latitude is a diagnostic of the start of a new cycle; the equatorial zone's decline is a complementary indicator.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prominence latitude zones and their phase behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: For prominences there are two zones in each hemisphere; each point in the curves represents the mean latitude of each zone throughout the year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpret the lower-latitude prominence zone as one that approaches the equator and dies out just before or at sunspot minimum; the higher-latitude prominence zone increases its latitude rapidly and dies out at or a little after sunspot maximum. Base latitude determinations on published Memoirs/Bulletins (e.g., Kodaikanal Observatory reports).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use corona form (from eclipse reports) as an index of solar activity
rubrics_metrics.description: The form which the corona takes at total eclipses indicates the condition of solar activity: a polar form with streamers all around indicates maximum, an equatorial or 'wind-vane' form indicates minimum, and intermediate or 'square' shapes indicate intermediate stages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collect corona-form data from individual eclipse-expedition reports and compile them (as Dr. Lockyer did). Represent corona forms with distinct symbols in time-series plots. Use corona-form changes alongside sunspot and prominence metrics to assess activity phase.

rubrics_metrics.name: Combine multiple indicators to infer cycle phase and predict minima/maxima
rubrics_metrics.description: All the solar phenomena described (sunspot areas and latitudes, prominence latitudes, corona form) together indicate the state of solar activity and can be used to predict phases such as approaching minima.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Synthesize evidence from area, latitude, prominence-zone behavior, and corona form to make cycle-phase statements (e.g., the paper concludes activity is waning and predicts a minimum in 1924 or 1925). Treat predictions as contingent on the combined dataset quality and provisional values.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use and collate published observational datasets; note provisional values
rubrics_metrics.description: The data for determining the state of the activity of the sun are published separately year by year in various volumes from different sources, and are only brought together, probably with some difficulty, by research workers who wish to use them for particular inquiries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When compiling multi-indicator time series, cite and cross-check the original sources (e.g., Monthly Notices, Kodaikanal Observatory Memoirs and Bulletins). Explicitly mark provisional values and be cautious when using recent, incomplete data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Miscibility testing for essential oils: use critical solution temperatures
rubrics_metrics.description: Instead of testing solubility by measuring the volume of aqueous alcohol required to obtain complete solution of a measured volume of oil, take the critical solution temperatures with definite mixtures of alcohol and water.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This critical-solution-temperature method is more sensitive for indicating small composition changes in oils; be aware that the critical solution temperature can vary markedly with time as the oil is kept.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider diffusion and grain-size interactions in annealing treatments of castings
rubrics_metrics.description: Diffusion at high temperatures may take place simultaneously with grain-growth, while at low temperatures it promotes a breakdown in the grain-size; these results have been applied to the annealing treatment of castings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Account for coupled diffusion and grain-growth effects when designing annealing schedules; understand that grain-boundary migration and grain-size changes affect material properties (e.g., specific gravity variations) and final microstructure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Select materials appropriate to high-temperature locomotive components and account for fusion limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Superheated steam as used on locomotives generally leaves the superheater at a temperature of 340°C; certain packing rings may fuse when temperatures rise to 425°C. Examples of satisfactory materials: M.R.A.1 alloy for piston valve fittings and cylinder relief valves, a phosphor-bronze for piston tail rod bushes, and McNamee rings for piston rod packing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose alloys and packing materials based on operating temperatures and shock conditions; prefer nickel-brass for by-pass valves subject to shock but consider economy (malleable iron/steel castings) and be mindful of fusion points for white-metal packings at higher temperatures.
